newsitem.title: USA: Florida Hurricane Fund cancels $500 mln bond sale.
newsitem.headline: Florida Hurricane Fund cancels $500 mln bond sale.

text.p: The Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund has cancelled plans to issue $500 million of revenue bonds, at least until after the 1997 hurricane season, the fund's attorney said Wednesday.
The fund had planned to seek approval from the state Board of Administration Wednesday for the taxable, pre-event bond sale.

The item was pulled from the agenda because the fund is awaiting two key rulings -- a bond validation from the Florida Supreme Court and an Internal Revenue Service letter ruling that could authorize it to issue tax-exempt debt.
The court validation for the bonds is required by the statute that established the fund. Fund attorneys submitted their briefs in February but the court has not yet ruled.
"Even if the validation were to come tomorrow, we would be out of time," fund attorney Cindy Gokel said.
She said it would take at least 90 days to adopt the appropriate resolutions, draft the bond documents and make presentations to bond rating agencies and investors.
That would put the sale "right in the middle of the hurricane season and there's no way of knowing what the meteorological conditions would be at that time," Gokel said.
The hurricane season begins June 1 and runs through Nov. 30.

Fund managers initially considered a pre-storm bond issue, in part to familiarize investors with the debt. But that would have had to be taxable because the proceeds would be invested until a major hurricane made it necessary to draw down the fund.
But the fund recently submitted a request to the IRS for a ruling on the tax-exempt status of its bonds, Gokel said.

"If we get a favorable ruling from the IRS, that changes the complexion for any decision to do a pre-event issue," Gokel said. "As for the possibility that we will get a favorable ruling fom the IRS before the end of the hurricane season, my guess is zero. It is our tax counsel's guess it will take six to nine months."
She said the intent of the bond issue was intended "to maximize the ability of the fund to meet its obligations."
The Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund is a trust fund administered by the state Board of Administration and acts as a sort of reinsurer.

Insurance companies that underwrite homeowners' policies for windstorm damage in Florida are charged a premium based on their exposure. They can choose copayments of 45 percent, 75 percent or 90 percent. Once a deductible has been met, the fund repays them for any losses above the copayment amount.
The fund will have about $2 billion by the end of December, Gokel said. The bond issue would have been its first.
Another state agency that deals with hurricane losses, the Florida Joint Underwriters Association, completed its first debt issue earlier this week with the sale of $300 million of tax-exempt notes.

That agency sells homeowners insurance to residents in high-risk coastal areas where commercial insurance is unavailable. That debt also was a "pre-event" issue designed to familiarize investors with the agency.
